findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive so block can be bypassed
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw value. User-supplied emails vary in case and surrounding whitespace while the blocked list is stored as-is, so Block@Example.com will not match block@example.com. An attacker can bypass an explicit block by changing case, defeating the purpose of the feature.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count loses updates
findings.body: should_block? does record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save. Under concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email two processes read the same count and write back the same value, losing one increment and clobbering last_match_at. Use an atomic counter update such as increment_counter/update_counters instead.

findings.title: Validator performs database writes on every validation
findings.body: EmailValidator#validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), which increments match_count and updates last_match_at and saves. Validation is expected to be side-effect free and can run multiple times per request or on unrelated validations, so statistics are inflated, extra writes happen on the signup hot path, and a failed/rolled-back user creation still leaves mutated blocked_email rows.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array on prototype is shared mutable state
findings.body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is defined in the object literal passed to extend, so the same array instance is shared by every instance of CreateAccountController. pushObject in createAccount mutates shared state, leaking one user's rejected/blocked emails into another controller instance and growing without bound. Initialize the array in init instead.

findings.title: Email validation will not refresh on rejectedEmails push
findings.body: emailValidation depends on rejectedEmails.@each but rejectedEmails is an array of strings mutated with pushObject. @each observes properties of array items, not array membership, so adding a newly rejected email may not invalidate the computed property. The dependent key should observe array membership such as rejectedEmails.[] or rejectedEmails.length.
